chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu Junada Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukharaq ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Warqa ibn Habashi ibn Junada Al-Saluli, companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), from Abu al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), regarding the statement of Allah:

Those are they of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts; so turn aside from them, for the Word of misery has already been ordained for them and the punishment has been ordained for them. And speak to them in their souls an eloquent word.

key_terms.صَاحِبِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Companion of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.قُلْ لَهُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ: Speak to them in their souls/inner selves

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'speak to them in their souls an eloquent word' in Quran 4:63 according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the divine strategy for dealing with hypocrites (munafiqun) by distinguishing between those whose inner disbelief is explicitly known to Allah and those who require subtle guidance. It highlights the concept of 'sabaq al-kalimah' (the precedence of the word of doom) for the former, while prescribing 'qawlan balighan' (eloquent speech) for the latter, emphasizing that effective da'wah must penetrate the heart rather than merely addressing the tongue. This interpretation aligns with Shia exegetical tradition, which views the 'eloquent word' as a profound, transformative message that resonates with the listener's inner reality.
